title: Ichimoku Strategy
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/0/body: A high-quality buy setup usually has all of these together: price **above the cloud**, **Tenkan above Kijun**, **Chikou above price** from 26 periods ago, and a **green future cloud** (Senkou A above B). The more confirmations, the better the odds.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/1/body: If some components are bullish and others bearish, the picture is **mixed**. In that case, many traders either stay out or enter with **smaller size**. Ichimoku was built to show whether its components **line up**.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/2/prompt: Put an Ichimoku trade in order, from the big picture to the details.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/2/items/0: Find the bias from price vs. the cloud
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/2/items/1: Get confirmation from the TK cross and Chikou
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/2/items/2: Wait for a pullback to the Tenkan or Kijun
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/2/items/3: Enter with a stop below the Kijun
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/2/explanati: First set the overall direction with the cloud, then confirm with the other components, and finally find a low-risk entry with a clear stop loss.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/3/prompt: How do you rate this Ichimoku setup?
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/3/options/0: Mostly bullish, but the future cloud is a warning; be careful
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/3/options/2: Everything lines up; buy with maximum size
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/3/explanati: Three components are bullish, but a red future cloud means the equilibriums ahead favor sellers. The picture isn't fully aligned, so smaller size or waiting makes more sense.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/4/statement: To enter with Ichimoku, any single component is enough on its own; you don't need to check the others.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/4/explanati: Ichimoku's strength is in its components lining up. A single component (like just a TK cross) gives lots of false signals.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/5/body: A common approach: in a confirmed uptrend, enter on a **pullback to the Tenkan or Kijun** and put your stop loss just **below the Kijun** (or, with more risk, below the cloud). Set your target with a risk-to-reward ratio.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/6/prompt: In this buy setup, where was the stop loss placed?
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/6/options/1: Below the bottom of the cloud
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/6/explanati: The stop loss (1.0838) is just below the Kijun (1.0850). If price closes below the Kijun, medium-term equilibrium has turned against buyers.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/7/prompt: Price is above a green cloud, the Tenkan is above the Kijun, and the Chikou is clear. Price has pulled back to the Kijun, and the last candle closed bullish. What's your call?
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/7/explanati: Every component lines up bullish, and price found support at the Kijun. It's a classic pullback in an uptrend. A continued rise is more likely, with a stop loss just below the Kijun.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l1/steps/8/prompt: Buying ETH on a pullback to the Kijun: entry 3,000, stop loss 2,940 (below the Kijun) and target 3,150. What's the risk-to-reward ratio?
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/0/body: When price **closes above the cloud** after a while below or inside it, that's called a bullish cloud breakout. The breakout is more reliable when the **candle body** closes outside the cloud, the future cloud is green, and the Chikou is clear too.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/1/body: After a breakout, price often comes back to test the **top of the cloud**, which now acts as **support**. Instead of chasing the breakout candle, many traders enter on this **pullback** with a stop loss below the cloud.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/1/tip: Not every breakout pulls back. If no pullback comes, don't chase price.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/2/prompt: Tap the first candle whose body closed above the cloud.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/2/explanati: The earlier candles closed inside the cloud, and one only poked its wick above it. This candle is the first real close above the cloud: a cloud breakout.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/3/statement: If only a candle's wick goes above the cloud but its body closes inside, it counts as a valid cloud breakout.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/3/explanati: A breakout is judged by the close outside the cloud. A wick that came back inside means buyers couldn't hold price up there.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/4/prompt: Price broke up out of the cloud. What's price's latest move?
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/4/options/0: A pullback to the cloud top after the breakout
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/4/explanati: After the breakout, price rose and has now come back to test the top of the cloud, but closed above it. That's a pullback to the broken zone.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/5/body: Some breakouts are **false**: price closes above the cloud but soon falls back inside. Breakouts of a **very thin** cloud, or breakouts the other components don't confirm, are more prone to this. That's why you always need a stop loss.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/6/prompt: Which cloud breakout is more reliable?
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/6/options/0: A close above the cloud with a bullish TK and a clear Chikou
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/6/options/1: Just a short wick above the cloud
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/6/options/2: A close above the cloud with a thick red future cloud
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/6/options/3: A breakout on a small candle in the middle of a range
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/6/explanati: A breakout the other components (TK cross and Chikou) confirm is better aligned. A lone wick, an opposing future cloud or a ranging market all raise the odds of a false breakout.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/7/prompt: After the cloud breakout, price came back to the top of the cloud, and the last candle is a strong bullish one. Which direction is more likely?
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/7/explanati: The top of the cloud acted as support after the breakout, and the bullish engulfing candle is buyers reacting. A continued rise is more likely. Stop loss below the cloud or below the pullback low.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/8/sentence: After an upside cloud breakout, the top of the cloud often acts as ___.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l2/steps/8/explanati: A zone that used to block price from rising often becomes the new floor after a breakout.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/0/body: Ichimoku works best in a **trending market**. In a **range**, the Tenkan and Kijun go flat and tangle, the cloud gets thin and twisted, and price keeps flipping above and below the cloud. The result is lots of **false signals**.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/1/body: All Ichimoku lines are built from **past data**, so its signals usually come **after a move has started**. That's fine for following trends, but it warns you late in fast reversals.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/2/prompt: Price is swinging above and below a thin cloud and a flat Kijun. How is this market for an Ichimoku strategy?
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/2/options/3: Best time for a TK cross
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/2/explanati: Price is swinging around a flat Kijun and a thin cloud. That's a range, and Ichimoku signals (like crosses and cloud breaks) turn out false a lot here.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/3/statement: Like other trend tools, Ichimoku has lag.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/3/explanati: Every component is built from past highs and lows or closes, which is why signals arrive a bit after a move starts.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/4/prompt: The market is ranging, the cloud is thin and twisted, and the Tenkan and Kijun are tangled. What's the most sensible move?
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/4/options/0: Trade less or wait for a break out of the range
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/4/options/2: Raise your leverage to make up for it
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/4/options/3: Remove your stop loss since the market is calm
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/4/explanati: In a range, Ichimoku loses its edge. Trading less or waiting for a clear trend saves you from false signals and back-to-back losses.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/5/body: The story goes that **9, 26 and 52** date from when Japan's work week was **6 days**. Crypto trades 7 days a week, so some traders try other settings like 10, 30, 60. No setting is magic; test it first.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/6/pairs/2/m: Signal comes after the move starts
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/7/prompt: Wrap-up: which situation is better for an Ichimoku trade?
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/7/options/0: Price above a thick green cloud, bullish TK and a clear Chikou
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/7/options/1: Price inside a thin cloud with flat lines
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/7/options/2: A bullish cross below a thick red cloud
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/7/options/3: Price flipping above and below the cloud every day
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/7/explanati: The first option is a clear trend with aligned components. The others are either a range and indecision, or a signal against the overall bias (a weak bullish cross below the cloud).
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/8/sentence: Ichimoku gives lots of false signals in a ___ market.
lessons/ichimoku-u3-l3/steps/8/explanati: Ichimoku is a trend system. When there's no trend, its lines tangle and false signals pile up.
